text:
Maria: Quick heads-up — the inbound dashboard is showing a +3.2x spike in ‘webinar’ leads yesterday around 15:10 UTC. Noticed this in the weekly KPIs view, but GA shows a smaller bump. Pinging @Jamie to check sample rate and filters. https://redwood.app/dashboards/inbound/kpis
Jamie: metrics-bot flagged a surge at 15:11, I’m pulling raw events now. Can you drop the dashboard link with the filters Maria?
Maria: here — default time window + source=webinar. I think someone switched the UTM fallback rule yesterday during the launch posts.
metrics-bot: [alert] inbound-rate-surge — inbound_count over baseline: 320% at 2026-02-12T15:11:00Z. Sample rate: 5% -> 100% detected on source=webinar subset.
Jamie: confirmed — sample_rate ingestion flag flipped for the webinar stream between 14:58–15:05. We only sampled 5% normally; the temporary pipeline change caused full ingestion for that partition. Raw counts (15:00–15:20): 2,340 events (raw) vs expected ~730 rescaled.
Aaron: ok that explains the dashboard delta vs GA — GA still sampled but our events DB ingested full set. Are we double-counting anywhere in the routing?
Lee: looked at the inbound routing rules — no duplication. But the lead mapping job picked up two UTM fallbacks for ~18% of rows (utm_source null -> fallback1 + fallback2). That’s a separate bug in the parsing lambda.
Sasha: can we separate the issues: 1) ingestion sampling misconfiguration, 2) UTM fallback duplication? We need both fixed for weekly KPI story.
Jamie: agreed. Quick action plan:
- I’ll revert sample_rate flag to 5% for webinar partition (OWNER: Jamie, ETA: 20m)
- Lee to patch parsing lambda to dedupe UTM fallback logic and add unit test (OWNER: Lee, ETA: EOD)
- Maria to annotate the KPI dashboard with an incident note and exclude the affected hour from the weekly aggregate visualization for Friday review (OWNER: Maria, ETA: today 17:00)
- Aaron to coordinate comms in the launch channel and flag any downstream leads that may require reprocessing (OWNER: Aaron, ETA: 30m)
Jamie: snippet I ran to validate the partition volumes — paste into console:```sql
SELECT event_date, source, count(*) as cnt
FROM inbound_events
WHERE event_time BETWEEN '2026-02-12T15:00:00Z' AND '2026-02-12T15:20:00Z'
AND source = 'webinar'
GROUP BY event_date, source;
```
Lee: noted. I’ll add a dedupe condition on the fallback sequence and run against staging. Quick patch: add DISTINCT on fallback keys and assert length <=1 in unit tests.
Sasha: for attribution debate: should we backfill corrected counts or leave a note and present two views (raw vs normalized)? My vote: present normalized in KPI deck, keep raw as an audit trail.
Maria: agree — normalized for decision-making. Jamie/Lee please produce corrected aggregates and a short note in the KPI slide explaining methodology.
Aaron: scheduling — let’s do a 15-min sync at 16:30 to confirm fixes and what we show on Friday’s KPIs. I’ll create a calendar invite and add the launch channel summary.
metrics-bot: [info] sample_rate reverted by Jamie at 2026-02-12T15:25:42Z.
Jamie: reverted and re-ingested the 15:00 partition with correct sampling flag. I’ll run a quick reconcile job and post the before/after counts in this thread when done.
Lee: patch PR opened: github.com/redwood/ingest/pull/482 — tests added. Requesting review from @Jamie.
Jamie: ACK, will review now. Early reconcile shows normalized webinar leads for the hour ~ 760 (vs dashboard 2340 raw).
Maria: perfect — once recon is in we’ll update the KPI dashboard and note the correction. Thanks everyone.
Sasha: capture decision for Friday KPI deck: show normalized counts, one-line footnote describing sampling misconfig + UTM dedupe fix.
Aaron: will draft the slide text and pull the reconciled numbers when Jamie posts them.
Jamie: posted reconcile: before: 2340 raw, after normalized: 747. Reprocessing mark: reprocessed_partition_id=20260212-15.
Maria: updating dashboard note now. ETA 16:50.
Aaron: closing loop — comms posted in #launch-channel and follow-up to sales ops to ignore the false surge.
Maria: thanks team — we’ll include postmortem snippet in Friday’s KPI review. :thumbsup:
